measures.note: After the last phrase the closing chord opens into a rising line: G, A, B, D.
A suspended D7 that resolves. It is the cue for the singers, who start on the next beat.

written.name: Flowing lead-in
written.summary: Four measures that echo the shape of the tune, pass through a diminished chord, and pause on D7 before the first note.

measures.note: A small turn around the note D over a rising G arpeggio.
The line reaches the high G over C; the bass then rises a half step to C sharp diminished.
The diminished chord resolves to G over D, and the line walks down to G.
Two chords in thirds, A minor nine and D7, leave the ear waiting for G.
The key lift. It is written here in the key of the song and played in the new key: the dominant seventh of the new key, with a line that climbs to its root.
The chord waits for two beats; the pickup follows in the new key.

endings.name: Amen
endings.summary: Two held chords, the four chord and then home: the sound of a sung Amen.

measures.note: The four chord, C, held for a whole measure.
Home: the G chord, held.

endings.name: Rising arpeggio
endings.summary: The G chord climbs through two octaves in eighths and comes to rest at the top.

measures.note: The right hand climbs G, B, D twice over; the left hand follows with its own arpeggio.
The last chord, high and soft.

endings.name: Gospel Amen
endings.summary: The four chord turns minor over the home bass note, a triplet roll climbs the G chord, and a last soft chord closes.

measures.note: C over the bass note G; on the last beat E falls to E flat, the minor four chord.
Home, then a triplet roll up the G chord to the high D and G.
The same chord once more, soft, in the middle of the keyboard.

endings.name: Grand close
endings.summary: Full chords in both hands: home, the four chord over the same bass, home, and a last chord at the top of the keyboard.

measures.note: G, C over G, G: only the two inner notes of the right hand move. The left hand keeps its octave.
The final chord, an octave higher and as loud as the song gets.

endings.name: Jazz close
endings.summary: A major seven chord a half step above home slides down into G with its sixth and ninth.

measures.note: A flat major seven: C, E flat and G over A flat. Every note is a half step from where it is going, or already there.
G with its sixth and ninth: B, E and A in the right hand.

fills.summary: The melody exactly as printed. Where it waits, the right hand answers with single notes: an arch over the long note in measures 7 and 8, and another under the final note.

measures.note: Fill: the D chord as an arch above the long note: F sharp, A, F sharp, D.
Fill: the line comes down through C, the seventh of D7, and turns up into the melody note.
The ending: an arch through the G chord while the last note rings.
The arch comes to rest on the melody note.

accompaniment.summary: Sustained chords: one three-note chord per measure, held while the left hand keeps its pattern. Over the long note and at the end the right hand plays an answering figure.

measures.note: The right hand plays the pickup with the singers, so they find their first note.
One chord per measure, held for all three beats.
Fill: the chord, then an arch up to A and back while the singers hold their note.
Fill: D7, a small turn below it, and a pair of notes that leaves room for the B of the singers.
The ending: an arch through the G chord.

arrangements.name: One step further
arrangements.summary: Same chords as the score. The arpeggio reaches a tenth, and the left hand rolls in eighths whenever the melody holds a long note.
tips: Practise the left hand alone at tempo 60 until the reach from the fifth to the tenth feels relaxed.
In measures 7 and 15 the melody stands still, so let the left hand sing there and keep it quiet elsewhere.

patterns.name: Tenth arpeggio
patterns.description: Root, fifth, then the third one octave up instead of the root. One changed note makes the chord sound open and warm.

patterns.name: Rolling eighths
patterns.description: Climb through the chord in eighth notes and turn back at the top. Use it while the melody holds a long note.

measures.note: Tenth arpeggio: the last note is 3' instead of 1'.
Your usual pattern, so the new one stands out against it.
The melody holds one note for five beats, so the left hand takes over the movement.
The seventh (7) appears inside the roll and pulls towards G.
Ending on the seventh leads the ear into the C chord.
Single notes only: bass D, then B rising to C, which falls back to B in the last chord.
Close with all three notes together.

fills.summary: The melody as printed. Over the long note the right hand adds double notes that rise through the D chord and come back down through D7.

measures.note: Fill: sixths and a fifth rise through the D chord, one on each beat, above the rolling left hand.
Fill: C with F sharp, the two notes that make D7, then a third lower, and the melody note.

accompaniment.summary: Rocking pairs: two notes at a time, a third or a fourth, on every beat, moving between two positions of the chord.

measures.note: The right hand plays the pickup with the singers, so they find their first note.
Two notes on every beat: the lower pair on beat one, the upper pair on beats two and three.
Fill: the pairs rise through the D chord, one position on each beat.
Fill: D7 comes back down, starting with C and F sharp, the two notes that define it.

arrangements.name: Walking bass
arrangements.summary: A waltz texture: one bass note, then two notes together. Inversions let the bass move by step instead of jumping from root to root.
tips: Play only the first note of every measure and listen to the bass line as a melody of its own.
Keep the two-note chords lighter than the bass note.

patterns.name: Bass and pair
patterns.description: Bass note on the first beat, fifth and octave together on the other beats.

patterns.name: Slash-chord bass
patterns.description: Keep the same pair on top and put the third of the chord in the bass. G/B sits one step below C, so the bass walks.

measures.note: G/B: the bass steps up from G through B to reach C in the next measure.
The bass steps back down from C to B.
Em replaces G: it shares two notes with G, and its bass E walks down to D.
D7/C puts the seventh in the bass. It wants to fall one step, to the B of G/B.
The bass stays on B while the pair changes to include the seventh.
The bass walks E to D and stays there; the last pair holds the two notes that define D7.

fills.summary: The melody as printed. Where it waits, a second line walks by step, the way an alto moves under a held soprano in a hymn.

measures.note: Fill: a line climbs by step from the long note to the high G.
Fill: the line walks back down, E, D, C, A, and meets the melody on B.
The ending: an inner voice dips to E and returns to G.

accompaniment.summary: A descant: one slow line of single notes above the tune, a long note and a short one in most measures. The seventh in measure 10 resolves down by step.

measures.note: The right hand plays the pickup with the singers, so they find their first note.
A single line above the tune: D for two beats, then E.
Fill: the line circles F sharp and reaches up to A while the singers hold their note.
Fill: it steps down through D and C and returns to D.
F natural is the seventh of G7; it falls to E in the next measure.
F sharp, the leading note, rises to the final G.

arrangements.name: New chords
arrangements.summary: Several printed chords are replaced: a secondary dominant, a suspended chord that resolves, and an Amen ending.
tips: Learn the shell shape 1 7 3' on Em7 first; the A7 in the next measure uses exactly the same shape.
Listen for the single note that moves when Dsus4 turns into D7.

patterns.name: Shell voicing
patterns.description: Root, seventh, and the third one octave up. Three notes are enough to show the whole colour of a seventh chord.

patterns.name: Suspend, then resolve
patterns.description: Hold back the third of the dominant by playing the fourth, then let it fall one step.

patterns.name: Amen ending
patterns.description: Place the IV chord over the home bass note before the final chord, the way a sung Amen closes a hymn.

measures.note: G7/B turns the home chord into a dominant of C and puts the leading note B in the bass.
Em7 stands in for G. The melody notes G and B both belong to it.
A7 is the dominant of D, the chord that follows. The hand shape is the same as in the previous measure.
Dsus4 delays the arrival: the fourth (G) replaces the third.
The suspended G falls to F sharp and the chord finally sounds complete.
The bass arrives home on G, but the chord above is still C. The real ending waits one more measure.
The Amen resolves.

fills.summary: The melody as printed. Over the long note the right hand plays the suspended fourth and lets it resolve, as the left hand does.

measures.note: Fill: G and A, the notes of the suspended chord, above the long note.
Fill: the suspended G falls to F sharp, and the line continues down through C and A to the melody.

accompaniment.summary: Syncopated chords with an added second: struck on beat one, on the 'and' of two, and on beat three, the rhythm of a modern worship ballad.

measures.note: The right hand plays the pickup with the singers, so they find their first note.
G with A in place of B: the added second gives the open, modern sound.
Fill: the suspended chord, then its notes G and A an octave higher.
Fill: F sharp, the resolution of the suspension, then the chord without C, so it does not rub against the B of the singers.
The C chord over the home bass: the Amen, before the final G.

arrangements.name: Alberti bass
arrangements.summary: A classical broken-chord figure in even eighths: lowest note, then the two upper notes in turn.
tips: Practise each chord as a block of three notes before breaking it up.
The first note of every measure is the bass; give it slightly more weight than the rest.
Measures 8 and 9 put the seventh and then the third in the bass. Hear how the bass falls C to B.

patterns.name: Alberti figure in three
patterns.description: The chord close together: lowest note, highest, then middle and highest twice. Six even eighths fill a measure of three.

patterns.name: Open figure
patterns.description: The same idea with the root an octave lower, for a fuller sound on the home chord.

measures.note: Open figure: root at the bottom, third at the top.
Close figure on C, one position for the whole measure.
G with B in the bass, so the bass can step up to D.
D7 with its seventh, C, in the bass. That note must fall to B.
And it does: G over B.

fills.summary: The melody as printed, with runs in sixteenths where it waits: a scale up and back, a broken chord, and a rising scale at the end.

measures.note: Fill: a scale runs up from the long note to the high A and back, over the plain Alberti figure.
Fill: the run continues downward, then breaks the D7 chord and arrives on the melody note.
The ending: the scale of G rises a full octave under the last note.

accompaniment.summary: A second voice in thirds and sixths over the Alberti bass, with a scale run over the long note and another at the end.

measures.note: The right hand plays the pickup with the singers, so they find their first note.
Two notes held for two beats, then a lower pair on beat three.
Fill: a scale runs up to the high A and back while the singers hold their note.
Fill: C with F sharp for D7, two passing notes, and a third below the B of the singers.
The ending: the scale of G rises a full octave.

arrangements.name: Gospel waltz
arrangements.summary: Octaves in the bass, a passing diminished chord, and a secondary dominant: the sound of this hymn in a gospel church.
tips: Play the octave with a relaxed, heavy arm and the eighths that follow lightly.
Measures 3 and 4 are the heart of the style: C, C sharp diminished, G over D. Practise them as one gesture.
Let the tempo breathe a little at the end of each line.

patterns.name: Octave and roll
patterns.description: An octave on the first beat, then the upper chord notes as rolling eighths.

patterns.name: Passing diminished chord
patterns.description: Between the four chord and the home chord, the bass rises by half steps: C, C sharp, D.

patterns.name: Secondary dominant
patterns.description: A7 is not in the key of G. It is the dominant of D and makes the arrival on D stronger.

measures.note: G7 over B: the seventh, F, appears and the bass prepares the step to C.
C sharp diminished on the third beat; the melody note E belongs to it.
The diminished chord resolves to G over D.
E minor seven replaces G for the second line of the verse.
A7, the dominant of D. Its C sharp is the note outside the key.
The seventh in the bass again, falling to B.
A minor and D7, the two-five of G, replace G over D.
The bass is home, but the chord above is C: the Amen is on its way.

fills.summary: The melody as printed, with gospel answers: a triplet roll, a chromatic slide into the melody, and an Amen in both hands at the end.

measures.note: Fill: a triplet rolls up the D chord and lands on a third. The left hand plays two notes together on beat two, so the hands do not pull against each other.
Fill: C with F sharp for D7, then A slides through A sharp into the B of the melody.
The ending: the right hand joins the Amen with the C chord on beat two.

accompaniment.summary: Backbeat chords: the left hand has beat one, the right hand answers on beats two and three. Over the long note it plays a triplet roll and a chromatic slide.

measures.note: The right hand plays the pickup with the singers, so they find their first note.
Nothing on beat one: the chords answer the octave of the left hand.
Only the top note moves for the passing diminished chord: C falls to B flat.
Fill: a triplet rolls up the D chord on beat three. The left hand plays two notes together there, so the hands do not pull against each other.
Fill: D7 at the top of the roll, then A slides through A sharp towards the B of the singers.
The Amen: the C chord over the home bass.

arrangements.name: Grand octaves
arrangements.summary: A broad, festive accompaniment: an octave in the bass on the first beat and full chords on the other two, with an octave walk-up where the melody waits.
tips: The leap from the octave to the chord is the whole difficulty; practise it slowly and without looking.
Change the pedal on every first beat.
Follow the dynamics so that measure 9 is clearly the loudest point.

patterns.name: Octave and chords
patterns.description: The root in octaves, then the full chord twice. The foundation of a grand hymn accompaniment in three.

patterns.name: Octave walk-up fill
patterns.description: While the melody holds, repeat the chord in eighths and let octaves climb step by step into the next chord.

patterns.name: Four-note final chord
patterns.description: Root, fifth, octave and tenth together. If the reach is too wide, roll the chord from the bottom.

measures.note: Fill: the melody holds for five beats, so the chord repeats in eighths on the last beat to drive forward.
Fill: the chord with the seventh in eighths, then octaves E and F sharp that walk up to G.
The final chord spans a tenth.

fills.summary: The melody as printed, on top of full chords. Over the long note both hands climb through the positions of the chord like a fanfare.

measures.note: Fill: the D chord rises one position on each beat, and repeats in eighths with the left hand.
Fill: D7 comes back down in two positions while the bass walks up in octaves.

accompaniment.summary: Four-note chords with the lowest note doubled at the top, in a long, short-long rhythm. Over the long note both hands play a fanfare.

measures.note: The right hand plays the pickup with the singers, so they find their first note.
Long, short-long: beat one, the eighth before beat three, and beat three.
Fill: the D chord, held, then repeated in eighths with the left hand.
Fill: D7 comes down through two positions while the bass walks up in octaves.
The loudest point: the chord moves up a position.

arrangements.name: Jazz waltz
arrangements.summary: A jazz-waltz reharmonization: a bass note, then a two-note shell, with sixth chords, two-five-one chains, and rootless thirteenths.
tips: The rhythm is bass on one, shell on two, silence on three. Count it aloud before adding the melody.
The shell is the seventh and the third of the chord (written 7 3'). Find it for G6, Em7, A9 and D7 first.
Play quietly; the colour of these chords carries without force.

patterns.name: Bass, then shell
patterns.description: The root on the first beat, the seventh and third together on the second, held through the third.

patterns.name: Two-five-one
patterns.description: D minor and G7 are the second and fifth steps of C; they turn the arrival on C into an event.

patterns.name: Rootless thirteenth
patterns.description: Seventh, third and thirteenth without the root. The melody or the previous bass note supplies the rest.

measures.note: G6 instead of G: the sixth, E, adds warmth without a seventh.
The two-five of C. The melody note B is the thirteenth of D minor.
C major seven, then the passing diminished chord a half step higher.
G6 with D in the bass completes the rise C, C sharp, D.
A9 is the dominant of D; the melody note B is its ninth.
Fill: A minor seven delays D7 by a measure; on the last beat the fifth and seventh are played one after the other to keep the pulse under the held note.
On the last beat the chord drops its root and adds the thirteenth, B, the note of the melody.
The two-five of G under the last line of the verse.
The final chord: G with its sixth and ninth.

fills.summary: The melody as printed, answered by two arpeggios: down A minor seven, then up D9 into the melody note.

measures.note: Fill: the notes of A minor seven fall from the long note: C, A, G, E.
Fill: D7 rises through F sharp, A, C and E, the ninth, and settles on B.

accompaniment.summary: Rootless voicings in the Charleston rhythm: on beat one and on the 'and' of two. The left hand has the roots, so the right hand plays thirds, sixths, sevenths, and ninths.

measures.note: The right hand plays the pickup with the singers, so they find their first note.
E, B and D over the G of the left hand make G6.
G, B and C sharp: the seventh, ninth, and third of A9.
Fill: the A minor seven chord, then a line that falls from D to G.
Fill: F sharp, C and E make D9; on beat three F sharp and B, the thirteenth, with the singers.
A, B and E: the ninth, third, and sixth of the final chord.
